reply_text:
**I’d block the merge on one authorization bug.**

**[P1] `src/guard.js:12` — View-only shares can edit unlocked documents.**
`share.mask & WRITE === WRITE` is parsed as `share.mask & (WRITE === WRITE)`, effectively checking bit `1` (`READ`), not `WRITE`.

Confirmed:
- A viewer (`mask: READ`) gets `canEdit(...) === true`.
- A WRITE-only share gets `0` (denied), despite having edit permission.

Use `hasRight(share.mask, WRITE) && !share.locked`, consistent with the other guards. Add regression tests for an unlocked viewer being denied and a WRITE-only share being allowed; the existing editor test passes accidentally because editors also have READ.

All six existing tests pass. I also checked all 16 rights masks for permission behavior, switch toggling, and distinct-user ownership transfers; no other bugs surfaced in those checks.

No files changed.
